t: Tradition holds that Christ showed Gebre Meskel Lalibela Jerusalem and told him to build a second Jerusalem in Ethiopia, and the churches' layout and names are widely taken to represent the holy city.
Their dating is disputed: tradition gives them to Lalibela's reign, Buxton thought the work ran into the 14th century, and Phillipson argues that some began as Aksumite-era structures of 600–800.
Carved from the top down out of the rock, they follow local building traditions of Aksumite origin and remain in daily use for worship and pilgrimage.
dyk: Francisco Álvares, who saw the churches in the 1520s, swore by God that all he had written of them was true, fearing that otherwise he would not be believed.
ev: According to local tradition, an Agew family called the Zagwe founds Roha, the later Lalibela
Gebre Meskel Lalibela begins his reign, to which tradition dates the churches
The Fra Mauro map, made in Venice, is the first European publication to name the place, as Lalabeda
The Portuguese priest Francisco Álvares visits the churches twice and describes them
Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi lays waste the district; the Futuh al-Habasha says he burned one of the churches
Haile Selassie makes a pilgrimage to the churches during the Second Italo-Ethiopian War
The churches are first included on the UNESCO World Heritage List
Shelters funded by the EU are put up over five of the churches as a temporary protection

f.made: Traditionally ascribed to King Gebre Meskel Lalibela of the Zagwe dynasty (r. c. 1181–1221); more likely shaped in several phases, the work perhaps running into the 14th century (David Buxton), with some churches possibly first carved between 600 and 800 (David Phillipson)
f.form: Eleven churches cut downward out of scoriaceous basalt with hammers and chisels, four free-standing monoliths and seven joined to the rock, linked by trenches and tunnels in groups north and south of the town's river Jordan, at around 2,480 m
f.where: Lalibela, a town in the Lasta district of the Amhara Region, Ethiopia; in use by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church
f.known: churches carved from the living rock; a layout representing Jerusalem; Biete Giorgis, the Church of Saint George; the Lalibela Cross of Biete Medhane Alem; pilgrimage at Genna and Timkat; doors and windows in the Aksumite style
